title.narrative: Skill Up! Unlocking success in Green Skills Development for Youths in Sierra Leone

description.narrative: (This is a follow-up project from SLE 1075 Skill UP)- Youth farmers attain diverse green skills;increase their incomes from self-employed agricultural work and entrepreneurship training; Young men and women increase their incomes from self-employed and employment in solar installation and maintenance; Youth attain knowledge and skills in climate change advocacy.

Outcome: The economic stability and decent income generation of vulnerable young people have improved through profitable employment or self-employment, resulting in living incomes, increased food, and nutrition security.

The project will target 700 direct participants, comprising 53% females (400 individuals) and 47% males (300 individuals), out of these numbers 10% will comprise persons with disabilities. These participants fall within the age range of 15 to 35 and belong to vulnerable, disadvantaged, and marginalized groups. A total of 3,010 indirect participants (the national average household size is 4.3) members of households associated with the direct participants will indirectly benefit from the support provided.At an institutional level, the indirect target groups include the personnel of relevant Government Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs). Eight (8) personnel from the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MAFS), four (4) staff members each from the Ministry of Youth, 4 from Ministry of Trade, 8 from the Ministry of Technical and Higher Education, 4 from the Ministry of Marine and Natural Resources, The National Youth Commission (NYC) in each region, and TVET Coalition. Furthermore, eight staff members from each district, city, and district councils, and 5 local authorities from each district, will be targeted.
